# TypeS

> A domain-neutral enterprise semantic type system: a canonical layer between physical enterprise systems (databases, REST APIs, legacy platforms) and their consumers (applications and AI agents), so a consumer can ask for an object, its relationships, its provenance, and the actions it can perform, without knowing which system produced the answer.

TypeScript monorepo (npm workspaces). Open standards throughout: JSON
Schema 2020-12 for the canonical type representation, MCP for the
AI-agent surface, OAuth/OIDC for identity. Not a clone of the Palantir
Ontology or C3 AI Type System, though conceptually similar in ambition.
Read [`docs/why-typesys.md`](docs/why-typesys.md) before assuming this is
the right tool for a given problem — it names when *not* to use it too.

## Start here

- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md): the full documentation index — tutorial, how-tos, reference, explanation.
- [docs/why-typesys.md](docs/why-typesys.md): when to use this, when not to, comparison to GraphQL federation / a hand-rolled BFF / Palantir/C3.
- [docs/quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md): clone to a working query in ten minutes, every command verified against this exact repo.
- [docs/how-to/start-a-project.md](docs/how-to/start-a-project.md): build your own application on TypeS in its own repository — install without npm, one bootstrap module, and where a console tool, web API, MCP agent, or in-process AI workflow plugs in.
- [docs/for-agents.md](docs/for-agents.md): **read this if you are an AI agent about to call the MCP server** — exact resource URIs, tool call shapes, auth model, a full worked request/response example.

## Core concepts (in order of dependency)

- [docs/semantic-meta-model.md](docs/semantic-meta-model.md): the canonical contracts — Type, Property, Relationship, Action, ComputedProperty, Policy, DataSource, Mapping, audit/Event — with real field names, not aspirational ones.
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the layered architecture (Model → Registry → Runtime → Query/Actions → Adapters → Systems, Policy/Audit cutting across), with Mermaid diagrams.
- [docs/completeness.md](docs/completeness.md): an honest, kept-current inventory of what's fully built and tested versus a documented-but-unbuilt extension point. Read before assuming a capability exists.
- [docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md](docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md): the living, ranked list of what stands between this reference implementation and real production traffic (a real policy engine, a threat model, data classification, encryption, and more; load testing and multi-instance support are partly addressed by ADR-0025). Read before betting production traffic on any of it.

## Key source, if you need ground truth rather than prose

- `packages/core/src/runtime/runtime.ts`: `SemanticRuntime` — the single boundary every consumer (human app or AI agent) goes through; input validation, policy, cache, rate limiting, tracing, and audit all happen exactly once, here. Policy is decided per object on its stored attributes (ADR-0030), so `query` results contain only rows the caller may read — a short or empty page with a `nextCursor` is normal, unless the rule plans exactly, in which case it is pushed into the adapter's filter and pages are full (ADR-0038). Every policy and classification decision is audited, `listActions` previews included (they share `invokeAction`'s gate); `packages/core/test/audit-completeness.test.ts` pins the call sites of the non-auditing primitives.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/input-validation.ts`: `InputValidator`, `semanticQuerySchema`, `QueryLimits` — query shape + size limits (default page 100, max 1000) and Action input checked against each `inputSchema`; failures throw `InvalidInputError`. The MCP `query` tool advertises this same schema, so change it here, not in `mcp-server`.
- `packages/core/src/registry/registry.ts`: `SemanticRegistry` — validates and composes Type/Action/Relationship definitions.
- `packages/core/src/model/`: every meta-model type, as actual TypeScript, always more current than any doc describing it.
- `packages/mcp-server/src/`: the MCP server — `resources.ts` (browsing), `tools.ts` (governed Actions + `query`), `auth.ts` (identity resolution), `http-transport.ts` (Streamable HTTP), `bin.ts`/`bin-http.ts` (stdio/HTTP entrypoints).
- `packages/redis/`: `RedisCache` and `RedisRateLimiter` — the shared state that makes several replicas behave as one (ADR-0025). Optional, env-gated tests (`REDIS_URL`).
- `packages/auth-oidc/`: real OIDC/JWT identity resolution — a drop-in `IdentityResolver` for `mcp-server`'s auth parameter.
- `packages/encryption/`: `EncryptingAdapter` — field-level encryption at rest as a decorator around any `Adapter` (AES-256-GCM, HMAC blind indexes for equality, refused range/sort/search/aggregate on encrypted fields), plus the `KeyProvider` seam, a `LocalKeyProvider` keyring, `WrappedKeyProvider` for KMS-wrapped data keys on a lease (ADR-0037), and `EncryptedCache` (ADR-0036). Optional, never a core dependency.
- `packages/kms-aws/`: `AwsKmsKey` — an AWS KMS key as `WrappedKeyProvider`'s `KeyEncryptionKey`, over a structural client interface (no SDK dependency). Emulator test gated on `KMS_ENDPOINT`.
- `packages/policy-cedar/`: `CedarPolicyEngine` — a drop-in `PolicyEngine` running Cedar in-process (WebAssembly), with a reference schema + policy set for both demo domains in `examples/` and a parity suite against `AbacPolicyEngine`. Optional, never a core dependency.
- `packages/adapter-postgres/`, `packages/registry-store-postgres/`: real PostgreSQL-backed implementations of `Adapter`/`RegistryStore` — both optional, env-gated, never a dependency of core.
- `packages/domain-airforce/`: the reference vertical-slice domain (Aircraft/Component/MaintenanceEvent/WorkOrder) — the pattern every new domain follows.
- `packages/domain-hospital/`: a second, unrelated domain (Patient/Provider/Appointment) proving that pattern generalizes — no changes to `packages/core` or `packages/mcp-server` needed.
- `docs/adr/`: 48 architecture decision records, one per major/hard-to-reverse choice, each with alternatives actually considered and rejected — the single best way to understand *why* something is shaped the way it is instead of some other reasonable way. 0024 records the decision to document, not close, the production-readiness gap (the ranked list itself lives in docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md); 0025 records the multi-instance design. 0026 (adapter-call resilience), 0027 (query DSL extensions: sort, projection, aggregation, full-text search), 0028 (relationship resolution beyond foreign keys: byJoinTable, byCompositeKey, bounded traversal), and 0029 (deployment artifacts: Dockerfile, docker-compose, reference Kubernetes, /healthz + /readyz) are all implemented and Accepted. 0030 (row-level authorization: policies decide on the object's own attributes, `query` decides per returned item and drops denied rows, member policies narrow rather than replace, deny-biased enforcement) is Accepted. 0031 (a Cedar `PolicyEngine`, `@typesys/policy-cedar`, in-process via WebAssembly, proven decision-for-decision identical to the ABAC engine) is Accepted. 0032 (data classification: `Identity.clearance` vs Type/member/value markings under a pluggable `ClassificationScheme`, enforced beside the policy engine, derived data inheriting markings) is Accepted. 0033 (field-level encryption at rest: an `EncryptingAdapter` decorator, AES-256-GCM + HMAC blind indexes, a `KeyProvider` seam with keyring rotation) is Accepted. 0034 (classification defaults: `DEMO_LINEAR_CLASSIFICATION` renamed from `US_CLASSIFICATION`, and an explicit `DENY_MARKED_DATA` default — marked data denied until a scheme is configured) is Accepted. 0035 (record-bound `tsenc2` envelopes: every ciphertext bound to its record, writes name the record, legacy `tsenc1` refused outside a migration, `reseal` migrates and re-keys) is Accepted. 0036 (sensitive-data caching: `Cache.confidential`, `Adapter.sensitiveFields`, encrypted and marked data and anything computed from it kept out of non-confidential caches, `EncryptedCache` for Redis) is Accepted. 0037 (KMS-backed keys: `WrappedKeyProvider` unwraps data keys at startup or refuses to start, leases them so revocation takes effect within `maxKeyAgeMs`; `AwsKmsKey` in `@typesys/kms-aws`) is Accepted. 0038 (authorization planning: `PolicyEngine.plan?` returns a sound over-approximating `AuthorizationPlan` — always/never/predicate(exact, limitations)/unknown; ABAC helpers plan from the rule structure; plans are pushed into `query`'s adapter filter and, when exact, admit `aggregate`; the post-read check stays; `rowSecurity`, runtime-only audited `explainQuery`, `checkPlanConformance`) is Accepted. 0039 (Cedar planning via `isAuthorizedPartial`: residuals translated by shape, unknown shapes weakened to `true`, a possibly-erroring subterm or a non-trivial `forbid` costing exactness, attribute-bearing Types exact only with `schemaConformantData: true`) is Accepted. 0040 (`Adapter.canFilter` for exact in-store filtering, `EncryptingAdapter` answering for deterministic fields; the Postgres adapter compiling filters to parameterized JSONB SQL — exact, or a superset re-checked with `matchesFilter` — and paging in SQL when exact) is Accepted. 0041 (security labels v2: `ClassificationScheme` is `decide({ subject, markings, context })` + `join(markings)`, decided on the join and on every marking alone; reference `securityLabels` scheme — levels, compartments, REL TO/NOFORN, CUI as its own regime, accreditation) is Accepted. 0042 (every audit row names the runtime operation — the outermost call — it was written under; a nullable `operation` column in Postgres) is Accepted. 0043 (`PolicyDecision.faults`: a rule branch that fails to evaluate is recorded, audited as `details.faults`, and counted in `typesys.policy.faults`, even under an allow) is Accepted. 0044 (Postgres numeric conditions are supersets bounded in exact `numeric` arithmetic by the neighboring doubles, never claimed exact) is Accepted. 0045 (`telemetryIdentity`: `"none"` | `"clear"` (default) | `{ mode: "pseudonymous", key }` — a keyed HMAC in `typesys.identity.pseudonym`) is Accepted. 0046 (`securityProfile: HIGH_ASSURANCE_V1`: versioned guarantees checked at construction — exact row security, aggregation only through `planAssurance: "structural"` plans, no clear telemetry identity, managed keys, no `demonstration` schemes, no unknown options — downgrades refused; never asserts `schemaConformantData`) is Accepted. 0047 (no raw identifiers in telemetry: `telemetryIdentity` also governs object ids — `typesys.object_pseudonym` — and span error messages, class name only unless `"clear"`; the MCP server's spans follow it via `runtime.redactsTelemetryIdentifiers` and never record the `?token=`; under a profile, engine faults other than `anyOf alternative N failed to evaluate` are audited as `external-policy-fault`; custom extensions are the trusted computing base) is Accepted. 0048 (a missing object is not found: `ObjectNotFoundError extends NotFoundError` from `getObject` and from the source of `getRelationship`/`getProvenance`, raised only after the policy decision so a denied caller is told nothing; a dangling reference is left out of a relationship or include) is Accepted.

## Running things

```bash
npm install && npm run build && npm test   # Postgres/Redis tests skip cleanly without DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL
npm run lint:install && npm run lint       # type-aware ESLint (isolated in tools/eslint — see below); CI fails on any error
npm run typecheck                          # type-checks tests and scripts too — `npm run build` only covers src
npm run smoke:mcp                          # real stdio MCP server, full discover-to-invoke script
npm run smoke:mcp-http                     # the same script over a real HTTP transport
npm run benchmark                          # SemanticRuntime latency/throughput, in-memory + Postgres
npm run load-test                          # N server processes under concurrent MCP load (REDIS_URL to share state)
npm run demo                                # interactive web app at http://localhost:4000
```

## Conventions for coding agents changing this repo

- **Before calling a change done:** `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck`, plus `npm run smoke:mcp` if you touched `mcp-server` or `SemanticRuntime`. CI runs all of these.
- **Linting lives in `tools/eslint/`, on purpose.** typescript-eslint needs TypeScript's JS API, which the TypeScript 7 used for the build doesn't ship, so the linter has its own `package.json` pinning TypeScript 5.9. Type information comes from `tools/eslint/tsconfig.lint.json`, which maps `@typesys/*` to each package's source (no build needed) and also backs `npm run typecheck`; add new top-level TypeScript folders to its `include`. Don't move ESLint into the root `devDependencies`: npm refuses the peer-dependency conflict. Install it once with `npm run lint:install`; auto-fix with `npm run lint:fix`.
- **Validate input at `SemanticRuntime`, never in a transport.** New public runtime methods that accept caller JSON should go through `InputValidator`, the same way they go through the policy engine, so apps, the demo HTTP API, and MCP agents all get identical checks.
- **Adapter calls share one budget per request.** `getAdapter` returns a view gated by the current call's `maxConcurrency` semaphore (an `AsyncLocalStorage`), so nested fan-out can't multiply it. Get adapters through `getAdapter`/`ctx.getAdapter`, never from `this.adapters` directly, or the call escapes the budget.
- **Shared state must go through the interfaces.** Anything that must agree across replicas (cache, rate limits, registry, audit) sits behind `Cache`/`RateLimiter`/`RegistryStore`; never add process-local state that changes behavior across instances without a shared implementation and a multi-instance test (see `packages/redis/test/multi-instance.test.ts`).
- **Query results are paged by default.** `query` without `limit` returns `QueryLimits.defaultLimit` (100) items. Adapters always receive a concrete `limit` and must honor it and return `nextCursor` when more remain.
- **User-visible behavior changes need a changeset** (`npm run changeset`) and, where relevant, an update to `docs/completeness.md` / `docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md`.
